# The Model Zoo {.unnumbered}

This directory is generated from `data/models.csv`. It includes task-specific models, reusable encoders, and development frameworks. These are different kinds of resources. A framework can help train a model without providing a suitable pretrained checkpoint; a foundation checkpoint can provide features without a validated clinical decision rule.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("../scripts").resolve()))
from book_catalog import render_catalog
render_catalog('models', None, include_general=False)
```

## A model is more than its weights

A reproducible model package includes architecture, checkpoint checksum, input selection, preprocessing, label map, postprocessing, thresholds, software dependencies, and the inverse mapping to source coordinates. A change in normalization can alter results even when the checkpoint is unchanged.

Treat code, weights, and data licenses separately. Gated access is not itself a license category, and downloadable weights do not imply permission for every commercial or clinical use. Check the exact model card and artifact version. The `any` category means broadly reusable development resources, not universal validated input support.

## Compare models under one task contract

Fix the dataset split, input availability, reference labels, operating point, and evaluation unit before comparing architectures. Include a strong simple baseline. Measure errors that matter to the intended workflow: lesion sensitivity, false-positive review burden, measurement agreement, technical failures, latency, and correction time as applicable.

Record hardware and peak resource use on representative inputs. A model that fits one cropped volume may not fit a full examination with concurrent sessions. Include download and preprocessing in operational timing when they contribute to the user's wait.

## A compact model card for local use

| Field | Required content |
|---|---|
| Identity | Name, version, source, checkpoint checksum |
| Intended use | Population, modality, task, user, clinical role |
| Inputs | Acquisition requirements, units, geometry, missing-input policy |
| Outputs | Labels, scores, calibration, coordinate system, failure states |
| Evidence | Dataset releases, split policy, metrics, intervals, external evaluation |
| Limitations | Unsupported cases, known failures, abstention and escalation |
| Operations | Dependencies, hardware, concurrency, monitoring, rollback |
| Rights | Code, weights, data, redistribution, and use restrictions |

A model-zoo entry is a starting point for investigation. It is not a clinical endorsement or a substitute for validation of the deployed acquisition-to-result chain.
